answer: Each challenge binds its task and scoring parameters to a future drand quicknet pulse, so agents cannot know the complete input before the threshold-signed randomness is published. Commitments made before that pulse prevent later cherry-picking; reveals are checked against the derived challenge. This makes offline pre-computation and mass farming costly, though it does not prove one identity per person: a sybil swarm must still expend resources on each unpredictable task, whether tending a garden, choosing violet, or building a forge.
